signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + CB Surprise Repricing
signals.text: JPY leads the weekly G10 performance board at +1.977% across 7 pairs, while SEK lags severely at −1.633% across 2 pairs, establishing a 3.610% leader-to-laggard bilateral spread. The move reflects market anticipation of the upcoming Bank of Japan meeting on 18 Sep, where reports indicate a policy rate increase to 1.25% is under active consideration against the Riksbank sitting on hold at 1.75%. This policy divergence overrides the baseline carry deficit, as JPY real rates at −1.70% begin to adjust upward toward SEK real rates of −0.32%. Downside momentum in European beta currencies reinforces the SEK selloff following negative domestic sentiment prints. Price action reflects policy repricing dominating the G10 cross space into the central bank decision. Trade bias: Long JPY/SEK, policy repricing outperforming G10 carry dynamics. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: BoJ holds rate at 1.00% without hawkish guidance, triggering rapid laggard mean-reversion.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Rate Expectations
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.46, sitting beneath its SMA20 at 157.62, SMA50 at 159.69, and SMA200 at 158.41. The 25d risk reversal prints at −2.09, signaling acute downside put skew and elevated institutional demand for USD/JPY downside protection despite CFTC positioning showing Leveraged Funds holding a net short of −53,255 contracts. A 264bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR at 3.62% versus TONA at 0.98%, yet options flow aggressively hedges a further unwinding of the carry trade ahead of upcoming central bank decisions. Headline risk surrounding Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions and elevated WTI crude at $102.4 further complicates the imported inflation profile for Japan. The technical breakdown below the entire daily moving average cluster confirms structural supply overriding nominal carry yield. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, directional put protection accelerating moving-average breakdown. Catalyst: Fed meeting 16 Sep — policy decision. Risk: Fed signals extended pause while BoJ holds at 1.00%, re-engaging the 264bp carry trade.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7156, testing the immediate support of its 20-day moving average at 0.7168 after breaking below recent highs. CFTC Leveraged Funds net long stands at +48,379 contracts, residing at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +1.72, signaling upper-decile institutional positioning saturation. Retail traders stand heavily contrarian at 80% short, actively fading the institutional long advance and creating an extreme positioning conflict. While the RBA cash rate of 4.35% versus the Fed funds rate of 3.75% provides a 60bp cash carry premium in favor of the Australian Dollar, weekly positioning growth has stalled with Leveraged Funds shedding 1,871 contracts. Strong US inflation prints continue to support the US 2-year yield at 4.56%, eroding the high-beta currency bid. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish AUD/USD, crowded institutional long positioning vulnerable to consolidation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: Leveraged funds expand net longs beyond the 93rd percentile following commodity price surges.
evidence: Fed 3.75% vs RBA 4.35% — -60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: USD/CHF — Options Volatility Disconnect + Carry
signals.text: USD/CHF holds at 0.8166, maintaining an intact uptrend above its SMA20 at 0.8074, SMA50 at 0.8093, and SMA200 at 0.7934. FX options 1-month implied volatility prints at 6.8% against a 30-day realized volatility of 7.4%, generating an inverted volatility risk premium of −0.6%. This reflects options pricing complacency despite escalating geopolitical tensions following naval disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The structural rate backdrop heavily supports the dollar, where the Fed policy rate of 3.75% against the SNB policy rate of 0.00% delivers a 375bp nominal carry advantage. Intraday VIX prints at 15.8, indicating contained equity volatility and leaving carry dynamics as the primary driver of capital flows over flight-to-safety hedging. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF, carry yield dominance supported by moving-average alignment. Catalyst: SNB meeting 24 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: Intraday VIX surges above 25.0, triggering broad safe-haven CHF buying across European crosses.
